title: Seahorse: A Unified Benchmarking Framework for Spatiotemporal Event Modeling
claim: Diverse models answer the same prediction question in different forms, and one unified framework evaluates them all under a single protocol.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right with arrows, central panel contains three color-coded sub-cards
description: Three-part horizontal figure read left to right, linked by black arrows. The left green panel poses the question "When and where will the next collision happen?" and shows a New York City map with dark-to-light green dots for recent collisions, over a timeline ending at "now" and a dashed "?" marking the next event. The large central panel, outlined in black, carries the Seahorse seahorse logo and name. Beneath it are three tinted cards: purple "a rate of events" with an intensity heatmap, orange "a probability of the next event" with density contours, and blue "samples of the next event" with scattered blue points. The right gray panel, titled "one protocol", has a ruler with three colored markers for likelihood on one scale, and a scatter with a red star for next-event prediction. The eye goes first to the Seahorse logo.
caption: Overview of SEAHORSE. Left: the most recent collisions before “now” on one New York City test day. Middle: STPP models answer the same question in different forms, as an event rate, a probability of the next event, or samples of the next event; all three are illustrated with one simple self-exciting model on these events. Right: SEAHORSE evaluates them under one protocol (schematic).
abstract: Spatiotemporal point processes (STPPs) model event data in continuous time and space, with applications in mobility, epidemiology, and public safety. Recent neural STPPs span expressive intensities, density models, continuous-time latent dynamics, normalizing-flow spatial decoders, and score-based generative mechanisms. Yet comparison remains fragile because implementations differ in preprocessing, coordinate normalization, splits, likelihood conventions, and evaluation protocols. We present Seahorse, a unified framework for reproducible training and evaluation of STPPs. Seahorse provides an encode-evolve-decode interface and an executable benchmarking contract that standardizes dataset handling, tuning, raw-coordinate likelihood reporting, and run artifacts across classical baselines, neural likelihood models, continuous-time Neural STPP variants, and sample-based generative models. On 13 real datasets and 19 presets, no model dominates: likelihood, calibration, and next-event prediction favor different models, and the strongest models take from minutes to hours to train. Using HawkesNest as a controlled synthetic stress-test suite, we show how diagnostic benchmarking can probe neural STPP behavior under increasing spatiotemporal entanglement. Seahorse provides reusable infrastructure for comparing, diagnosing, and extending STPP models beyond implementation-specific leaderboards. The implementation, including preset configurations and reproduction scripts, is available at https://github.com/YahyaAalaila/seahorse.
